prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- Use the service that best matches the kind of place and level of support you want:
  - Airbnb — best for a mix of private rooms, unique stays, local hosts, and community features (Superhost badges). Good for experiences and short-to-medium stays.
  - Vrbo — best for whole-home rentals and family/group trips (fewer shared spaces). Often owner-managed listings for longer stays and group needs.
  - Booking.com — best when you want hotel-like flexibility (lots of apartments and hotels, pay-later/free-cancel options, large inventory and last-minute availability). Less “host” interaction.
- Compare the same property across sites (the same place sometimes lists multiple places) and pick the platform with the best price/cancellation/guest-protection terms.
- To find a good host: vet reviews, verify identity and responsiveness, ask targeted questions, and never pay or communicate outside the platform.

How to choose between the platforms (quick guide)
- I want a unique local stay or to interact with a host → Airbnb.
- I want an entire home for family/group and fewer shared spaces → Vrbo.
- I want hotel alternatives, flexible cancellation and pay-at-arrival options or last-minute choices → Booking.com.
- If security deposit, insurance, or 24/7 support is a top priority, compare the platforms’ policies for your destination; Booking.com and Airbnb have different protections.

What to check on every listing (checklist before you book)
- Total price breakdown (nightly + cleaning + service + taxes + security deposit).
- Cancellation policy and refund terms (especially for international travel).
- Recent reviews (last 6–12 months) and reviewer profiles.
- Host status: Superhost/Top Host/Verified vs newer/unvetted.
- Response rate & speed (many platforms show response rate).
- Photo quality and consistency with the description.
- Exact sleeping arrangements and maximum occupancy.
- Location: map view, address (if available), Street View of neighborhood, distance to transport/attractions.
- Amenities you need (Wi‑Fi speed, kitchen equipment, washer, AC/heating, parking).
- House rules, check-in/check-out process, and noise restrictions.
- Local short‑term rental rules / permit notices (some cities ban or restrict rentals).
- Security/deposit details and whether there’s an on-site manager.
- Read at least the last 10 reviews and pay attention to repeat complaints.

Red flags to avoid
- No reviews or only very old reviews for a listing marketed as “new.”
- Host asks you to communicate or pay outside the platform.
- Vague or contradictory photos and descriptions.
- Host is slow or evasive answering straightforward questions.
- Repeated negatives in reviews about cleanliness, safety, or last-minute cancellations.
- Listings with unrealistic pricing or unusually low cleaning/service fees.
- “Instantly book” but host profile is empty or unverified.

How to vet a host (questions to ask before booking)
Send a short, polite message before you book. Example template you can copy and modify:
“Hi — I’m [name]. I’m traveling with [number and relationship, e.g., 2 adults] for [purpose, e.g., vacation/work] from [dates]. A few quick questions: is the calendar accurate? How is check-in handled? Is there parking? What’s the Wi‑Fi speed? Any house rules we should know about? Do you require a security deposit or ID during check-in? Thanks!”
Other useful questions:
- Who manages the property if there’s an emergency or maintenance issue?
- Are any areas off-limits?
- Are cleaning supplies and toiletries provided?
- Is the neighborhood noisy at night?
- Where do we pick up keys / is there self check-in?

How to read reviews effectively
- Focus on recent reviews and recurring themes (cleanliness, accuracy, communication).
- Look for detailed reviews with context (who stayed, what went wrong/right).
- A few minor complaints are normal; multiple reviews citing the same problem are a deal-breaker.
- Check guest photographs when available — they can confirm accuracy.

Booking strategy and safety
- Always pay through the platform (Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com) — never transfer money direct to a host outside the platform.
- If cancellation flexibility matters, filter by “free cancellation” or choose refundable rates.
- Consider travel insurance for nonrefundable bookings or expensive trips.
- Take photos of the space on arrival and message the host about any damage within 24 hours if needed.
- Save all messages and receipts from the platform.

Extras for long stays or remote work
- Ask about monthly/weekly discounts, utility caps, and heating/AC costs.
- Verify reliable internet and request a speed test if needed.
- Confirm where to set up mail/packages and whether there’s a workspace.

Bottom line
- Use Airbnb for local flavor and host interaction; Vrbo for whole-home family/group stays; Booking.com when you want hotel-like flexibility or last-minute options.
- Whichever platform you use, screen listings with the checklist above, communicate and document everything through the platform, and avoid off-platform payments.

If you tell me your destination, travel dates, party size, and priorities (price, location, whole home vs shared, pets, work/Wi‑Fi), I can recommend a more specific search strategy and a short message to send to hosts.
